cases.description: An empty command sequence produces empty state.
Starting a run is durable but does not execute it.
A single tick executes a successful action.
Ticks without work and after completion do not call the service.
Forward references run in dependency order, while output retains definition order.
A join waits for both branches and executes once.
A blocked first definition does not block independent later steps.
Ready runs execute by creation order, independent of run ID sorting.
Step initial deadlines equal run creation time; ticks do not advance time.
The largest valid amount reaches the external service unchanged.
Step IDs must be unique.
All dependency references must exist.
A multi-step cycle is rejected.
A dependency list is a set, not a multiset.
Boolean true must not be accepted as integer amount one.
Unknown step fields are rejected rather than silently ignored.
Unknown command operations are rejected.
At least one step is required.
Completed run IDs cannot be reused.
A committed transient schedules a retry and idle ticks cannot bypass its deadline.
The next attempt is eligible at the exact durable retry deadline.
Exhausting the budget blocks dependent and independent pending work.
With max_attempts one the first transient is terminal.
A waiting oldest run does not starve ready work in a later run.
Recovery resumes a durably begun attempt without consuming another attempt.
An applied effect lost before commit is replayed, not applied again.
Repeated recovery crashes preserve the original attempt and make no service calls.
A replay whose response is also lost can be replayed again safely.
An uncommitted transient consumes a service failure but not a new durable attempt.
Restart preserves a future retry deadline and does not call the service.
The last permitted attempt can recover a successful effect with its original number.
Cancellation before execution cancels every pending step and emits no effects.
Cancelling a completed run leaves its success and cancellation flag unchanged.
Cancellation reconciles an in-flight pre-effect crash by lookup without execution.
Cancellation preserves an already recorded effect and reports a cancelled run.
Cancellation removes future retries while preserving their durable deadline.
Cancellation retains completed predecessors but does not start their dependents.
A lost successful lookup is repeated; reconciliation remains durable and idempotent.
Crashing before cancellation lookup neither creates effects nor increments attempts.
A lost transient is reconciled as missing after cancellation, even if execution would now succeed.
Run and step pairs that collide under underscore concatenation remain distinct.
Failure and later cancellation of a terminal run do not stop a separate run.
Restart and observation never implicitly execute pending work.
An idle checkpointed tick does not crash the process.
Independent work can finish during backoff; recovery then unlocks a join.
An in-flight later step is recovered before an earlier step whose retry becomes due.
Cancelling after a branch effect keeps successful branches and prevents a join.
Cancelling an unknown run is an error.
Execution requires a live process.
Process availability is checked before cancellation run existence.
Restarting an already running process is an error.
Simulated time cannot exceed the defined integer bound.
Scheduling a retry past the time bound is an error.
Unknown fault injection names are rejected.
A second transient during recovery reuses the original attempt and schedules backoff from recovery commit time.
A successful independent branch and its effect survive another branch exhausting its retry budget; the join is blocked.
An individual advance argument above the static bound is INVALID_INPUT, distinct from runtime addition overflow.
